## San Juan, Argentina: a city between history and desert landscapes

San Juan is the capital of the province of the same name in western [Argentina](/argentina/), in the Tulum Valley at the foot of the Andes. The city makes a convenient stop between Mendoza and the natural areas of San Juan and La Rioja provinces. You can spend a day exploring its squares and museums before continuing to [Ischigualasto](/argentina/place/ischigualasto/) and [Talampaya National Park](/argentina/place/talampaya-national-park/).

What sets San Juan apart from Argentina's old colonial cities becomes apparent on its streets: broad avenues and much of the urban fabric date from the rebuilding that followed the devastating 1944 earthquake. The city's story unfolds through its surviving monuments and the more modern architecture of reconstruction.

## Why downtown San Juan looks modern

San Juan was founded in the 16th century. Its historic buildings suffered extensive damage in the earthquake of January 15, 1944, after which the city was rebuilt according to a new urban plan. Travelers expecting continuous blocks of colonial-era houses may therefore find San Juan surprisingly modern.

That history is a subject worth exploring in its own right. A walk through the central streets reveals the results of reconstruction and allows you to compare buildings from different periods. The city's history museum tells the story of the earthquake and how the provincial capital changed. Here, architecture is closely tied to people's lives and the history of engineering solutions in an earthquake-prone region.

## What to see in one day in the city

### Plaza 25 de Mayo and the cathedral

Plaza 25 de Mayo is the city's central square. Opposite it stands the Cathedral of St. John the Baptist (Catedral San Juan Bautista), built on the site of the former church destroyed by the earthquake. The modern building is especially interesting for its architectural departure from traditional colonial churches.

This is a convenient place to begin a walking tour before heading to the museums. Access to particular interior spaces and guided visits to the cathedral should be checked against the opening arrangements in effect on your travel dates.

### Domingo Faustino Sarmiento's birthplace museum

One of the most important historic addresses is Casa Natal de Sarmiento, the house where Domingo Faustino Sarmiento was born and lived. He was a 19th-century Argentine educator, writer and president. The early-19th-century house has been preserved as a historic monument and museum, with interiors, household objects and exhibits on the family's history.

This museum is rewarding for visitors who want to understand Argentine education and statehood through one person's biography. Unlike a general city tour, it offers the chance to examine documentary details at leisure.

### Museums, theater and cultural life

San Juan also offers a more contemporary cultural itinerary. Notable venues include the Franklin Rawson Museum of Fine Arts and the Teatro del Bicentenario. If your time is limited, choose the museum that best matches your interests and leave enough time for the journey to your next destination.

## From San Juan to Ischigualasto and Talampaya

San Juan often serves as the urban stop before a journey through geological landscapes. [Ischigualasto](/argentina/place/ischigualasto/) lies in the same province and is known as the Valley of the Moon, where important Triassic deposits containing ancient fossils are protected. [Talampaya](/argentina/place/talampaya-national-park/) lies in La Rioja province and is known for its towering red rock walls and organized excursion routes.

Together, the two parks form a single UNESCO World Heritage property. They offer different experiences: Ischigualasto is particularly associated with extraordinary sedimentary rock formations and paleontology, while Talampaya is known for deep canyons and imposing red cliffs. Traveling between them also involves considerable distances and road transfers, so it makes more sense to plan consecutive excursions rather than treat them as two neighboring city museums.

The Valle Fértil area is a convenient base for visiting the Valley of the Moon, allowing excursions to be spread across separate days. In hot weather or strong winds, it is particularly important to check excursion schedules carefully.

## San Juan on an Ada Tours itinerary

Our [“Argentina: Journey into the Prehistoric World” tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/) includes San Juan after Mendoza. Travelers arrive by bus from Mendoza, check into a hotel and discover the city. The itinerary then continues with a transfer to Valle Fértil and a visit to Ischigualasto, followed by Talampaya.

This combination reveals both the city's cultural history and the much older geological history of the nearby parks. If dinosaurs and desert landscapes are your main interests, allow enough time for the road journeys rather than squeezing the parks into a brief stop between cities.

## Practical advice: climate, transport and length of stay

This part of Argentina has a dry climate. Summer days can be hot, and temperature differences between daytime and evening can be noticeable. Comfortable shoes, water and sun protection are useful in the city. For park excursions, you will also want closed shoes and clothing for cooler or windy conditions.

One day of sightseeing in San Juan is often enough within a longer itinerary. Ischigualasto and Talampaya require additional time and road planning. Check the actual opening hours of individual museums and parks for your travel dates, as they may change.

## Frequently asked questions about San Juan

### Is this the same San Juan as the city in Puerto Rico?

No. This article is about San Juan in Argentina, the capital of a western province near the Andes and desert nature parks.

### Can I visit Ischigualasto from San Juan?

Yes. The city is a starting point for exploring the province. However, the distance is considerable, so it is more convenient to plan a dedicated excursion and consider accommodation in the Valle Fértil area.

### What is particularly interesting in the city center?

Plaza 25 de Mayo, the cathedral, Sarmiento's birthplace museum, and the story of reconstruction following the 1944 earthquake. These sights explain why a city founded in the 16th century looks so modern.

## Tours through San Juan: the city, the Valley of the Moon and red canyons

[San Juan](/argentina/place/san-juan/) sits at the foot of the Andes in western Argentina. The city is worth visiting for its museums, squares and the story of Domingo Faustino Sarmiento. On a longer journey, its principal advantage is the opportunity to connect [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) with [Ischigualasto Provincial Park](/argentina/place/ischigualasto/) and [Talampaya National Park](/argentina/place/talampaya-national-park/). In one stretch of the itinerary, the scenery shifts from vineyards to urban neighborhoods and Triassic landscapes.

In our catalog you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with San Juan among their main destinations. On our itinerary, the city features in the [13-day “Buenos Aires, Mendoza, San Juan, Puerto Madryn” journey](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/). This is a route through several distant regions of one country, not a stand-alone day trip to San Juan.

## How San Juan fits into a journey across Argentina

The complete tour lasts **13 days and 12 nights**. It begins in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), continues through the Mendoza wine region, and then reaches San Juan and its surroundings. The final section takes place on the Atlantic coast near [Puerto Madryn](/argentina/place/puerto-madryn/) and the Valdés Peninsula.

| Stage | What the itinerary includes |
|---|---|
| Day 6 | Bus from Mendoza, arrival assistance, hotel check-in and San Juan sightseeing |
| Day 7 | Transfer to Valle Fértil and excursion to Ischigualasto |
| Day 8 | Excursion to Talampaya National Park |
| Day 9 | Transfer toward the Atlantic coast via the airport |

A city tour is scheduled in San Juan after arrival. Sights named in the itinerary include the cathedral, the Franklin Library and the Félix Aguilar Observatory. An important distinction is that **days 7 and 8 are dedicated to nature parks**; the entire stop should not be imagined as several free days in town.

After the desert parks, the journey continues east with a flight to Trelew via Buenos Aires and a transfer to Puerto Madryn. The precise transport arrangements and included services should be checked on the full tour page; international and domestic air tickets are listed among the expenses not included in this offer.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_argentina_puteshestvie_v_doistoricheskij_mir}}

## What to see near San Juan

### Ischigualasto: paleontology and the Valley of the Moon

[Ischigualasto](/argentina/place/ischigualasto/) lies in the northeastern part of San Juan province. Its landscape, known as the Valley of the Moon, consists of rock layers that tell the story of life on Earth during the Triassic period. Early dinosaurs and other fossil vertebrates are studied here. Together with neighboring Talampaya, the park is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

On day seven of our itinerary, an afternoon visit to Ischigualasto is planned after the transfer to Valle Fértil. This works particularly well on a route through San Juan: the nature excursion is integrated into the sequence of transfers, and the day ends with a return to the hotel.

Visits inside the protected area follow designated routes with authorized guides. Visitors are not free to wander anywhere among the geological formations. It is best to treat access as part of a specifically organized excursion day.

### Talampaya: the canyon's red walls

[Talampaya National Park](/argentina/place/talampaya-national-park/) is in neighboring La Rioja province. What most distinguishes it from Ischigualasto are its long red canyon walls, dry riverbeds and rock art. The two parks are often combined on one journey, although they are visited on separate days.

Day eight of the itinerary is devoted to Talampaya. Following the excursion, travelers return to San Juan. This arrangement makes it possible to experience both World Heritage parks while maintaining the journey's principal transport sequence.

## Why this tour differs from an ordinary visit to San Juan

A short city break offers time for museums, historic buildings and local food. On our itinerary, San Juan plays another role: it links several geographically distant parts of Argentina. Before reaching it, travelers explore the wineries of the [Uco Valley](/argentina/place/uco-valley/) and the Andean foothills; afterward, they discover the Atlantic coast's wildlife.

The contrasting interests are important too. Mendoza focuses on winemaking and mountain scenery; San Juan brings urban culture and prehistoric landscapes; and [Puerto Madryn](/argentina/place/puerto-madryn/) offers coastal wildlife. The route combines substantial excursions of different kinds. For trips centered primarily on nature, browse our [wildlife-watching itineraries in Argentina](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/) when that themed selection is available.

This style of travel suits people comfortable with frequent hotel changes and time spent on transfers. If Ischigualasto is your main goal, consider whether you also want the other stages of the 13-day journey.

## When to plan the journey

Ischigualasto has a dry climate with substantial seasonal and day-to-night temperature differences. Argentine tourism sources describe March–June and September–November as comfortable periods for visiting the park. However, **these are not universally the best months for the entire 13-day itinerary**: on the Atlantic coast, whale and penguin watching follows different natural seasons.

When choosing dates, check separately which animals may be seen on the [Valdés Peninsula](/argentina/place/valdes-peninsula/), as the marine part of the tour includes a whale-watching boat trip from [Puerto Pirámides](/argentina/place/puerto-piramides/) and a visit to a penguin colony. If the desert parks take priority, San Juan's climate becomes a key consideration.

Pack comfortable closed shoes, sun protection, drinking water and clothing suitable for noticeable temperature changes. For the nature parks, knowing the visiting arrangements and length of transfers in advance matters more than choosing a city hotel solely for its location.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a proper guided tour of San Juan?

Yes. On day six of the 13-day trip, arrival assistance, hotel check-in and a sightseeing tour of San Juan are scheduled after the transfer from Mendoza. The published itinerary does not state a separate duration for this excursion.

### How long does visiting Ischigualasto and Talampaya take?

The itinerary assigns **2 consecutive days** to these parks: day seven to Ischigualasto and day eight to Talampaya. Both days also involve transfers, so it would be incorrect to treat them as two full, uninterrupted days inside the parks.

### Is this itinerary suitable for someone who does not go trekking?

It is a multi-day sightseeing itinerary involving car and bus transfers. Challenging mountain trekking is not listed as part of the San Juan visit. Walking distances, transport conditions and individual limitations should be considered for each excursion day.

### Can I visit only San Juan without Puerto Madryn?

The published 13-day itinerary includes both regions. If you want only the city and its neighboring parks, that is a different itinerary to discuss separately, not an automatically included shortened version of the existing tour.

To make your final choice, see the [full itinerary through San Juan](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/), including the day-by-day route, accommodation, prices and lists of included and additional services.

## San Lorenzo Nature Reserve: where to see Magellanic penguins in Argentina

San Lorenzo (Estancia San Lorenzo) lies in the northern part of the [Valdés Peninsula](/argentina/place/valdes-peninsula/), on the coast of Argentine Patagonia. Visitors come to watch Magellanic penguins on land as the birds move between nests, feed at sea and return to the colony. Open coastal steppe, low vegetation and Atlantic winds define the setting.

This is a destination in its own right on a wildlife itinerary. Travelers usually stay in [Puerto Madryn](/argentina/place/puerto-madryn/) before exploring Valdés, while [Puerto Pirámides](/argentina/place/puerto-piramides/) is associated with boat excursions and whale watching. The San Lorenzo colony offers a different experience: watching penguins from land. To see both whales and penguins, coordinate the order of your visits and the season for each species.

## When to visit the penguins

Magellanic penguins do not spend the entire year at their breeding colonies. According to the Valdés protected area's administration, the birds begin returning in September, lay eggs in October, and their chicks gradually become independent by February. The colony season ends by April. The number of birds and stages of breeding you can observe depend on the month and natural conditions.

| Period | What to expect |
|---|---|
| September–October | Birds return, prepare nests and lay eggs |
| November–January | Breeding season and care of chicks |
| February–March | Growing chicks and the gradual end of the season |
| April–August | Most of the colony is away from the coast |

The seasonal timetable and visitor access can vary between sections of the coast. If seeing penguins is the principal purpose of your trip, aim for the middle of the period when the colony is present and check access arrangements for your chosen date. Whales, elephant seals and orcas have their own seasonal windows; there is no guarantee of encountering every species on a single outing.

## How to organize a trip around the Valdés Peninsula

[Puerto Madryn](/argentina/place/puerto-madryn/) is a practical base for a journey through Atlantic Patagonia. From there, travelers head onto the peninsula, where wildlife viewing points are separated by long stretches of steppe. Plan driving, observation stops and the return journey as one route rather than several short city-style excursions.

Penguin watching at San Lorenzo can sensibly be combined with other Valdés sites if the season and agreed access permit. Boat trips from [Puerto Pirámides](/argentina/place/puerto-piramides/) depend on the weather and sea conditions. The land itinerary also needs time in reserve: strong winds are possible along the exposed coast, and road conditions and visiting arrangements should be checked before departure.

On our [Argentina itinerary through Mendoza, San Juan and Puerto Madryn](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/), a visit to San Lorenzo, lunch and penguin watching follow the boat excursion. The full list of services and sequence of days are given on the tour page.

## Wildlife-watching rules and what to bring

Penguins are wild birds living in a natural colony. Visitors must stay on authorized paths, follow guides' instructions, avoid feeding or touching animals, and never block their routes to burrows or the sea. Do not approach the birds too closely for photographs. Binoculars and a moderate zoom allow you to watch their behavior without disturbing the colony.

For Valdés, bring a windproof jacket, comfortable closed shoes, sun protection and drinking water. The wind can be noticeable even when temperatures are warm. Families with children should consider the length of the driving day and whether everyone can comfortably walk the full permitted route.

If your wildlife interests extend beyond one species, compare [nature and wildlife trips in Argentina](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/) and a route around the [Valdés Peninsula](/argentina/place/valdes-peninsula/). San Lorenzo offers land-based penguin watching; whales and other marine wildlife are observed at different sites and during different periods.

## Frequently asked questions about San Lorenzo

### Can you see penguins at San Lorenzo in winter?

During the Southern Hemisphere winter, the main breeding colony is absent. For a trip focused on penguins, plan primarily for the season from September into early autumn, and confirm the exact dates for the year you travel.

### Are San Lorenzo and Punta Tombo the same place?

No. They are separate colonies on the coast of Chubut province. San Lorenzo is on the Valdés Peninsula, while Punta Tombo lies farther south. They should not be used interchangeably when describing a specific route.

### Can San Lorenzo be combined with whale watching?

Yes, provided the season, weather and length of the trip allow both activities. Boat trips from [Puerto Pirámides](/argentina/place/puerto-piramides/) and the land-based penguin walk are separate activities with their own conditions.

### Should a visit to the colony be booked in advance?

It is sensible to check access and excursion availability in advance because this is a protected natural area with visitor rules. Do not assume unrestricted entry on any date or identical visiting hours throughout the year.

## Tours to San Lorenzo: Magellanic penguins on the Valdés Peninsula

[San Lorenzo Nature Reserve](/argentina/place/san-lorenzo-nature-reserve/) is in the northern part of the [Valdés Peninsula](/argentina/place/valdes-peninsula/), in Argentina's Chubut province. This is Atlantic Patagonia, a landscape of open steppe, low coastal slopes and a large colony of Magellanic penguins. For wildlife enthusiasts, the visit offers the chance to watch birds in their natural habitat, rather than simply admire ocean views from a lookout.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through San Lorenzo. On our itinerary, the site forms part of a [13-day journey through Argentina, including Mendoza, San Juan and Puerto Madryn](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/). San Lorenzo occupies part of one excursion day, while the complete tour also covers the capital, a wine-growing region and nature parks near the Andes.

**Important:** this is San Lorenzo on the Valdés Peninsula, near Punta Norte. It should not be confused with the town of the same name near Salta in northwestern Argentina, where the landscapes and excursions are entirely different.

## What the penguin-watching day includes

San Lorenzo is scheduled for **day 10** of the trip. After breakfast, travelers leave [Puerto Madryn](/argentina/place/puerto-madryn/) for the [Valdés Peninsula](/argentina/place/valdes-peninsula/). The day includes an introduction to coastal wildlife; animals mentioned in the itinerary include elephant seals, sea lions and penguins.

A boat trip to watch southern right whales is scheduled from [Puerto Pirámides](/argentina/place/puerto-piramides/). The stated duration of the boat excursion is **approximately 1.5 hours**. The route then continues to San Lorenzo for lunch and a walk among Magellanic penguins. Travelers return to Puerto Madryn in the evening.

| Part of the day | Main activity |
|---|---|
| Morning | Drive from Puerto Madryn to Valdés |
| Puerto Pirámides | Whale-watching boat excursion |
| San Lorenzo | Lunch and visit to the penguin colony |
| Evening | Return to Puerto Madryn |

This is the sequence of one particular itinerary, not a universal route for every visitor to the peninsula. Meeting times, conditions for boat departures and opportunities to see wildlife depend on the date and weather. It is particularly important to distinguish an excursion included in the plan from the possibility of actually seeing animals during your chosen season.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_argentina_puteshestvie_v_doistoricheskij_mir}}

## Why San Lorenzo is interesting for penguin watching

Magellanic penguins come to the Patagonian coast to breed. On the Valdés Peninsula, they occupy coastal areas, build nests and raise their chicks. Visitors see the birds among low shrubs and open steppe vegetation, very different from the familiar image of penguins surrounded by ice.

The Puerto Pirámides municipal tourism portal describes San Lorenzo as an estancia in the Punta Norte area, about **80 km from Puerto Pirámides**, with one of the area's largest colonies of Magellanic penguins. The estancia also has a history of traditional sheep farming. For travelers choosing this itinerary, however, the purpose of the stop is wildlife observation rather than a separate rural leisure program.

These are wild birds. Their presence, distance from paths and activity change throughout the season. When taking photographs, stay on the permitted route, do not block the animals' movements and follow your guides' instructions.

## When to go: penguins, whales and weather

### Penguin season

Magellanic penguins can generally be seen along the coast of Chubut **from September to April**. This is the regional season; the state of any particular colony on a given day depends on natural conditions. The birds first return and nest, then raise their chicks, and finally leave their breeding grounds toward the end of the season.

### Whale watching

The usual season for southern right whales on boat excursions from Puerto Pirámides is described by regional tourism authorities as **June to December**. Accordingly, the months when these two seasons overlap are generally the most suitable for combining both kinds of wildlife watching. Even then, specific numbers of animals, their proximity and suitable weather for boat trips cannot be guaranteed.

To compare different wildlife itineraries, browse our [Argentina wildlife-watching tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/) when that selection contains active offers. The wildlife calendar matters more than a general division into high and low tourist seasons: it determines which species make a trip to Valdés worthwhile.

## Preparing for a Valdés excursion

Journeys across the peninsula take place in open country, where winds can be strong and some roads are unpaved. Even in warm weather, pack a windbreaker, closed shoes, a hat, sunscreen and water. Additional warm layers are useful on the boat. Binoculars let you observe animals from a distance without approaching their resting places.

A sea excursion and a walk among penguins should not be treated as activities with identical operating conditions. The first depends on sea conditions and port operations; the second on land access and the colony's seasonal calendar. The protected area's administration advises checking forecasts, roads and seasonal wildlife access in advance. Transport, guiding, lunch and included services on the tour should be checked against the confirmed itinerary.

## Who this itinerary suits

This journey will particularly appeal to travelers who want to see contrasting sides of Argentina on one trip. Before reaching the Atlantic, the route passes through [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the wine region of [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/), [San Juan](/argentina/place/san-juan/) and the paleontological park of [Ischigualasto](/argentina/place/ischigualasto/). On the coast, the focus shifts to whales, penguins and marine mammals.

If your only goal is the San Lorenzo colony, the full 13-day program may be more than you need: it is designed to bring together several regions. But if you also want the Andes, wineries, unusual desert landscapes and Atlantic wildlife, this route is a much closer match.

## Frequently asked questions

### Where is San Lorenzo Nature Reserve?

On the Valdés Peninsula in Chubut province, near Punta Norte. A visit is usually arranged as part of a land excursion around the peninsula from Puerto Madryn or Puerto Pirámides.

### Does the tour include penguin watching?

Yes. The day 10 description explicitly includes lunch and a walk among Magellanic penguins at San Lorenzo. Their seasonal presence, however, remains a natural factor.

### Can I see whales on the same day?

The itinerary includes a boat trip from Puerto Pirámides lasting approximately 1.5 hours. Actual whale sightings depend on the season, weather and the animals' behavior; an excursion being scheduled does not itself guarantee an encounter.

### Do I need to travel for all 13 days just to visit San Lorenzo?

No. The natural attraction itself occupies part of one excursion day. **13 days is the duration of the entire published Argentina tour**, connecting Valdés with Buenos Aires, Mendoza and San Juan.

See the [“Argentina: Journey into the Prehistoric World” tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/) for the full day-by-day sequence, included services and payment conditions.

## San Telmo in Buenos Aires: old streets, a market, antiques and tango

San Telmo is a historic neighborhood of [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), south of the old administrative center. Cobbled streets, low houses with courtyards, wrought-iron balconies, antique shops, restaurants and small bars have survived here. Within the modern city, the neighborhood evokes Buenos Aires during the era of port trade and major waves of European immigration.

Walking is the best way to discover San Telmo. The market, [Plaza Dorrego](/argentina/place/plaza-dorrego/), Defensa Street, old buildings and cultural spaces are all close together. For a first visit, choose a few stops and leave time to enjoy the neighborhood itself.

## Defensa Street and historic buildings

Defensa Street connects the city center with the southern neighborhoods and Parque Lezama. It runs through San Telmo and is one of the main walking routes through historic Buenos Aires. Along it you will see buildings with interior galleries, antique shops and surviving architectural details from earlier periods.

Look out for the courtyards of older houses. Some are now occupied by small shops and galleries; others retain historic facades without admitting visitors. Whether you can enter depends on each building's rules: a private residence remains private even if it looks like a museum.

From here, you can continue along the street toward [Plaza de Mayo](/argentina/place/plaza-de-mayo/), linking San Telmo's everyday architecture with the capital's principal historic square.

## San Telmo Market: what is inside

Mercado de San Telmo stands at the intersection of Defensa and Carlos Calvo streets. The historic market opened in 1897. It was designed by architect Juan Antonio Buschiazzo, and its interior retains metal structures, arches and a roof with openings for natural light.

The market originally supplied food to residents of a rapidly growing immigrant city. Today, food stalls and dining options stand alongside antiques and small shops. You can explore the interior, stop for something to eat or simply wander through the aisles.

| Place | Why visit |
|---|---|
| Defensa Street | Historic facades and antique shops |
| San Telmo Market | Historic building and food |
| Plaza Dorrego | Cafés, old houses and the street fair |

Opening hours vary from one business to another. The market's existence does not mean that every stall is open every day or at the same time.

## The Sunday fair and tango

San Telmo becomes noticeably livelier on Sundays. An antiques fair takes place in Plaza Dorrego, with stalls and street performances extending into nearby sections of Defensa. The historic fair began in 1970 as a city initiative to sustain interest in the old neighborhood.

You can browse vintage objects, vinyl records, collectibles and handcrafted goods. The items on offer and the number of vendors change. Weekdays are better for relaxed photographs of the old neighborhood; Sunday suits visitors who want to experience busy street life.

San Telmo is famous for tango. However, a performance by a particular ensemble, a lesson or an evening show is not guaranteed on every walk through the neighborhood. Check their schedules separately and book tickets for indoor performances according to the venue's terms.

## Combining San Telmo with central Buenos Aires

A logical walking route begins at [Plaza de Mayo](/argentina/place/plaza-de-mayo/), then follows Defensa through the historic blocks to the market and Plaza Dorrego. In one walk, you can discover both the political and everyday history of the city.

If time allows, continue to Parque Lezama. But San Telmo deserves time of its own: its smaller details are easy to miss on a hurried bus tour.

On our [“Best of Argentina: 14 Days” tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/), the historic neighborhoods of Buenos Aires form part of a wider itinerary through the capital and other regions. For any particular tour, distinguish a general city sightseeing excursion and free time from an independently arranged market visit or evening tango show.

## Practical tips for walking around San Telmo

Wear comfortable shoes: sections of the cobbled streets are uneven, and you will be walking between the main sights. At the busy fair, keep an eye on your phone and bag, as you would in other popular urban areas.

If antiques and street performances are your priority, choose Sunday. For architecture, museums and quiet cafés, another day may suit you better. After dark, use reliable transport for your return and take the conditions on individual streets into account.

## Frequently asked questions about San Telmo

### Where is San Telmo?

In the historic southern part of Buenos Aires, not far from Plaza de Mayo and Defensa Street.

### When does the famous fair take place?

Traditionally on Sundays in Plaza Dorrego and neighboring streets. Check the exact hours and participating vendors closer to your visit.

### How is San Telmo different from La Boca?

San Telmo is known for its old urban buildings, market and antiques, while [La Boca](/argentina/place/la-boca/) is primarily famous for colorful facades and the culture of the Caminito area.

### Can I visit San Telmo without a guided tour?

Yes. The main streets and square are open for walking. A guide can help you better understand the history of the buildings and the neighborhood.
